80236.subject: 💰 The Funding: What has changed for crypto hedge funds since last October's crash?
80236.body:
Fund performance is mixed, investor interest is slowly returning, and some market problems remain.

The Funding ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by Yogita Khatri | Edited by Zack Abrams

Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 61st edition of The Funding ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) !

It's been nearly a year since last October's record crypto liquidation event ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding/2025-10-19-the-funding-crypto-vcs-unpack-the-largest-liquidation-event-in-history-and-whats-next-375220?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) , which wiped out more than $19 billion in leveraged positions. How have crypto hedge funds performed, and are they still struggling? I caught up with fund managers to find out what has changed for them and how much progress has been made on the problems the crash exposed.

Let's get into it.

*THE INSIDE VIEW*

*Crypto hedge funds, a year after the crash*

Nearly a year after the record liquidation event ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding/2025-10-19-the-funding-crypto-vcs-unpack-the-largest-liquidation-event-in-history-and-whats-next-375220?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) on Oct. 10, 2025, crypto hedge funds are still dealing with its effects. Market liquidity has not fully recovered, fund performance varies widely and managers see limited progress on some of the problems the crash exposed.

"The market never really got its depth back so books are thinner, market makers carry less inventory, and every sharp move has more air under it than it used to," said *Leigh Drogen, general partner and chief investment officer at Starkiller Capital.*

The flash crash wiped out more than $19 billion in leveraged positions. Earlier editions covered what went wrong, the pressure on markets that followed ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding/2025-11-30-crypto-correction-whats-next-380828?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) , how funds changed their strategies ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding/2026-05-31-the-funding-how-crypto-hedge-funds-are-navigating-weak-markets-403128?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) and whether a recovery was taking hold. ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding/2026-08-25-is-crypto-bear-market-over-412741?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

The recent rally has helped, but much of the market remains below pre-crash levels.
